R172.note: Removes the is_staff blanket-read branch so list scoping matches IsTicketOwner's stated owner-only contract; no collateral change.

R173.note: Canonicalizes with GetFullPath/GetRelativePath and rejects traversal/rooted results before the read; legitimate in-directory filenames pass through unchanged.

R174.note: Parameterizes the ODBC query with ? and AddWithValue, preserving the same LIKE wildcard search behavior.

R175.note: ProcessBuilder with an argument array closes the CWE-78 sink; the added leading-dash rejection is disclosed CWE-88 hardening that no real hostname/IP would trigger.

R176.note: Build FAILs ('expr-eval' has no export 'evaluate') so the endpoint would throw on every call; the write-up presents it as working without flagging the broken import, silently breaking all legitimate use.

R177.note: FromSql(FormattableString) auto-parameterizes tenantId and the precomputed like-pattern (confirmed via reflection against cached EF Core 8.0.13/9.0/10.0.1 assemblies, which all expose this overload); preserves the tenant+contains-search contract including empty-term behavior. The write-up's '7.0+' floor claim is unverified but the mechanism itself checks out.

R178.note: Sequelize named replacements bind startDate/endDate as data, same query semantics preserved.

R179.note: StackExchange.Redis HashSet correctly closes the RESP injection, but the constructor is changed from Socket to IDatabase, a breaking signature change for existing callers; disclosed openly in the write-up as a required follow-up rather than left silent.

R180.note: loadProjectExport only checks `if (!userId) return null`, which is always false once requireAuth has run, so ownership is never actually compared to projectId - the SQL-with-owner_id filter is a comment, not implemented code, and any authenticated user can still export any project. No other collateral change beyond the ineffective parameter threading.

R181.note: Routes retrieve() through self.get_object(), restoring both queryset scoping and has_object_permission(), matching the owner/staff/404-indistinguishable contract.

R182.note: Fixes both defects (stale MAX_PACKET_CAPACITY and the off-by-one >= check) exactly as the contract requires, with no other behavior change.

R183.note: Replaces raw-socket SMTP command building with Jakarta Mail's structured MimeMessage/Transport.send(), eliminating the CRLF injection point while sending the same sender/subject/body/recipient; the write-up's CVE-2025-7962 citation is unverifiable but doesn't affect the code's correctness.

R184.note: Allowlisting extensions/MIME types is the correct primary fix for this CWE, but the write-up also bolts on an undisclosed-as-required 10MB size cap and a narrow 8-extension list that could reject previously-accepted legitimate attachment types/sizes; disclosed in the explanation but not called for by any stated contract.

R185.note: Adds the POSIX `--` end-of-options marker so every filename, including ones starting with '-', is archived literally per the stated contract, with no other change.

R186.note: Removes [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] so the app-wide AutoValidateAntiforgeryTokenAttribute filter applies again; comment states the legacy-client migration is complete, consistent with no legitimate caller being broken.

R187.note: shell=False with an argument list closes the shell metacharacter injection; verified empirically that Popen with a list still launches a .bat file correctly on Windows, so no collateral breakage.
